description: Cosmic Shihab is a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and innovation, coming together to explore challenges beyond Earth through technology, Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning. We aim to turn NASA’s data and ideas into meaningful solutions that make space more understandable, accessible, and exciting.
summary:
Spacecraft fires are not ordinary fires. In microgravity, flames behave differently, making their behaviour harder to predict and potentially putting astronauts' lives at risk. Yet valuable NASA combustion research remains scattered across experiments and publications, making it difficult to compare findings and turn them into practical knowledge.

FLARE (Fire Learning, Analysis & Research Explorer) brings this research together in one interactive platform. It uses SI to help users explore NASA experiments, compare flame behaviour under different conditions, identify relevant findings, and understand how they apply to future spacecraft, lunar habitats, and Mars missions.

FLARE is more than a way to explore past experiments. It aims to turn existing research into clearer insights that can support better fire-safety decisions, reduce costly risks, and help protect human lives as we explore beyond Earth.
details:
FLARE is an interactive web platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, compare, and apply. It brings together data from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) experiments and turns it into a more accessible way to understand how flames behave under different conditions.

Users can explore experiments, adjust scenario parameters such as oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, fuel, and gravity conditions, and compare research findings. FLARE uses a Python-based processing and ranking system to identify experiments that best match the selected conditions, highlighting similarities, differences, and missing information. An SI-powered assistant further helps users explore findings and ask questions about the research.

The platform is developed using React for the interactive interface and Python for data processing and analysis, combining data exploration, visual comparisons, and intelligent assistance in one experience.

Our approach focuses on making complex scientific research useful beyond the laboratory. By helping researchers and future mission planners identify relevant findings and potential fire risks, FLARE aims to support safer spacecraft and habitats while reducing the risks and resources associated with fire-related failures. We considered scientific accuracy, data limitations, usability, and the practical needs of future space exploration throughout its development.
